newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani cotton rates up on short supply.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani cotton rates up on short supply.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates rose on Monday as supplies dwindled, fuelling speculation about the size of the 1996/97 (July-June) crop, dealers said.

They said prices were likely to remain firm despite an official statement that the crop would be above nine million 375-lb bales, against an earlier target of 10 million and last year's production of 9.96 million bales.
"There are no sellers in the market as supplies are getting thinner by the day," dealer Kishin Chand said.
In the kerb market, NIAB-78 variety was traded at 2,325 rupees ($57.80) per maund (37.32 kg), dealers said.
